hints.title: Substring Character Permutation Obstacle
hints.text: Generating all permutations of s1 yields factorial explosion. How can you compare character counts over a window of length len(s1) in linear time without rebuilding frequencies?

hints.title: Fixed Length Frequency Invariant
hints.text: A substring of s2 is a permutation of s1 if and only if its length equals len(s1) and its 26-character frequency count matches that of s1.

hints.title: Sliding Window Frequency Update Procedure
hints.text: Count frequencies of s1 and the first len(s1) characters of s2 in 26-element arrays. Track count of matching character frequencies. Slide the window one index right: add incoming character, drop outgoing character, update match count. If matches == 26, return True.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Fixed-size sliding window maintaining 26-element alphabet frequency array in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating permutations takes O(M!) time and sorting each substring takes O(N * M log M) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 26-element integer table uses constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Tracking matches count or comparing 26-length arrays directly in O(1) time per window step.
